cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Fluent in Nonsense
cards.instruction: Perform complete mastery of the strange logic while inventing each rule only when it becomes necessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave your sofa on the ceiling until I say otherwise. Which way did you turn the gravity dial?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Right. My landlord arrives in ten minutes. Can I turn it back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One number. Slowly. The dial accepts a correction only when I have finished saying its name. Six.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six clicked, but the armchairs are rising. Can we stop naming numbers?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can. The chairs have requested a hearing. You explain the sofa; I'll hear their objections one at a time. Nobody turns anything while I'm listening.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 grants B2 one dial correction on A spoken timing; A5 accepts B4 stopping request only by assuming authority over a newly invented furniture hearing.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 right-turn history and reversal request cause A3 limited reversal; B4 rising chairs causes A5 hearing and no-turn instruction.

relationship.evidence: B2 landlord deadline gives a tenant a credible need for rapid help; B4 suggests stopping an apparently worsening procedure.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 new chairs to expand A control from the dial to a hearing, delaying the repair while claiming mastery of the complication.

specificity.evidence: A1 ceiling sofa and gravity dial plus B2 landlord deadline establish the emergency; no literal courtroom or unseen official needs inventing.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 timed Six and A5 nobody turns while listening are speakable displays of authority; the hearing is an improvised explanation of rising furniture.
